title: From Financial Inclusion to Economic Empowerment: Union Minister Smt. Annpurna Devi Hails 12 Years of the Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana
subtitle: Over 59 crore Jan-Dhan accounts opened, with 56% belonging to women and 78% in villages and small towns
body_text:
Union Minister of Women and Child Development, Smt. Annpurna Devi has hailed the completion of 12 years of the Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana, describing its journey as one from financial inclusion to economic empowerment.
In a post on 'X' the Union Minister said that under the visionary leadership of the Hon’ble Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, the Jan-Dhan Yojana has connected crores of citizens – especially women and rural families – with the formal banking system, and built a strong foundation of financial self-reliance.
Sharing the achievements of the scheme, she said that more than 59 crore Jan-Dhan accounts have been opened, of which 56% belong to women and 78% are in villages and small towns. Deposits in these accounts have crossed Rs. 3.1 lakh crore, and Rs. 53 lakh crore has been transferred directly to beneficiaries through the JAM (Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile) trinity.
The Union Minister said that this is not merely a scheme for opening bank accounts, but a transformative journey of dignity, security and empowerment.

ministry.name: Ministry of Women and Child Development

enrichment.summary: Union Minister Annpurna Devi marked the 12th anniversary of the Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), highlighting that over 59 crore accounts have been opened, 56% held by women and 78% in rural/small-town areas. She noted deposits have crossed Rs. 3.1 lakh crore and Rs. 53 lakh crore has been transferred via Direct Benefit Transfer using the JAM (Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile) trinity.
enrichment.context: PMJDY, launched in August 2014, is the government's flagship financial inclusion scheme aimed at ensuring universal access to banking, remittance, credit, insurance and pension facilities, particularly for the unbanked poor. It underpins the JAM trinity—linking bank accounts, Aadhaar and mobile numbers—which enables leakage-free Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) of subsidies and welfare payments, and has been credited with reducing corruption in welfare delivery and improving women's financial autonomy through schemes like PM-KISAN, MGNREGA wages, and pandemic-relief cash transfers. The scheme's emphasis on women account holders also links to broader financial and social empowerment goals, as accounts in women's names have been used to channel targeted benefits and build savings habits. This release is a ministerial statement reiterating cumulative achievement figures on an anniversary rather than announcing new policy, but the updated statistics are useful reference data for understanding the scale and reach of India's financial inclusion drive.
